mark_split.label: Take the sine of both sides

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.115, chapter 10 INVERSE TRIGONOMETRIC FUNCTIONS, Short Answer question 9. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. A full mark is given to the domain and a full mark to testing the two candidates, because squaring creates a root here that the domain test alone does not remove. NOTATION: the book prints this question with the word arcsin; it is written here as Sin⁻¹ to match the notation used across the rest of this unit, and the mathematics is unchanged. Checked numerically to twelve decimal places: at x = 13 the left side equals 1.570796326795 = π/2, and at x = −13 it equals −1.570796326795, so −13 is rejected. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints eight short answers of which the student writes any six, at 4 marks each, under the 2026-27 pattern; Inverse Trigonometric Functions is an SAQ-only unit, so the paper gives it no Section-A and no Section-C slot. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this one — name each move in order, and say how you test the roots you find.

steps.label: Write the domain
steps.margin_note: First mark. Writing the domain first is what lets a wrong root be rejected later with a reason.
steps.memory_tip: Both arguments must lie between −1 and 1, so |x| ≥ 12 — the larger numerator sets the limit.

recall.must_convey: That both arguments must have size at most 1, giving |x| ≥ 12 and x ≠ 0.
accept: sin inverse needs its argument between minus one and one so modulus x must be at least twelve
the twelve over x condition is the one that decides it
write the domain before starting the algebra
domain modulus x twelve kanna ekkuva undali
x cannot be zero and its size is at least twelve
reject: take the sine of both sides

steps.why: Sin⁻¹ is only defined for values between −1 and 1, so x cannot be small. The condition |x| ≥ 12 already forces |x| ≥ 5, so |x| ≥ 12 is the one that counts.
common_mistakes: Starting the algebra without writing the domain.

steps.label: Take the sine of both sides
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The right side is a square root, so it is never negative — that single fact rejects one root at the end.
steps.memory_tip: sin(π/2 − θ) = cosθ, and cos(Sin⁻¹k) = √(1 − k²), always the positive root.
lines: Take the sine of both sides:

recall.must_convey: That one term is moved across and the sine is taken, turning the right side into cos(Sin⁻¹(12/x)) = √(1 − 144/x²).
accept: move one term across and take the sine, sine of pi by two minus theta is cos theta
the right side becomes the square root of one minus one forty four over x squared
cos of a sin inverse is the positive square root
sin pi by two minus theta ante cos theta
take the sine of both sides after shifting one term
heard_as: one forty four over x squared

steps.why: sin(π/2 − θ) is cosθ, and the cosine of a Sin⁻¹ value is the positive root, because Sin⁻¹ returns an angle in [−π/2, π/2].

steps.label: Square and solve
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Multiplying through by x² is safe because x ≠ 0 was written in the first step.

recall.must_convey: That squaring gives x² = 169, so the candidates are x = 13 and x = −13.
accept: square both sides to get twenty five over x squared equals one minus one forty four over x squared
multiply through by x squared so x squared is one sixty nine
the candidates are plus and minus thirteen
x squared one sixty nine, so plus or minus thirteen
squaring clears the root and gives a quadratic in x
reject: take the sine of both sides
the domain is modulus x at least twelve

steps.why: Squaring clears the root, but it can also create a value that does not satisfy the original equation, so both candidates must be tested.
common_mistakes: Giving only x = 13 with no test.

steps.label: Test both candidates
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The domain test alone does not reject −13, because 13 is more than 12; the sign test is what removes it.
steps.memory_tip: x = −13 passes the domain but fails the equation — squaring created it. Always put each root back in.
lines: but a square root is never negative, so it fails.

recall.must_convey: That x = −13 is rejected because it makes the left side negative while the square root is positive, leaving x = 13.
accept: both pass the domain but minus thirteen makes the left side negative while the root is positive so it is rejected
at minus thirteen the two inverse sines add to minus pi by two not pi by two
only thirteen satisfies the original equation
minus thirteen fail avthundi, only thirteen answer
put each candidate back into the original equation
reject: the domain is modulus x at least twelve

steps.why: x = −13 is inside the domain but was created by the squaring step. Both Sin⁻¹ values are then negative, so their sum is −π/2 and not π/2.
common_mistakes: Not writing the check for x = 13.
